video_title: Will Nikola Jokic LEAVE Denver? 👀 + Bucks Trading Giannis BEFORE the NBA Draft? | KOC x Tim Bontemps

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Oklahoma City Thunder face major roster decisions this offseason
quotes.excerpt: They have all these massive decisions to make. What are they going to do with Isaiah Hartenstein?
quotes.quote: I think you have to start with the Oklahoma City Thunder. They are coming off this series where they just lost to the Spurs. They have all these massive decisions to make. What are they going to do with Isaiah Hartenstein and Lu Dort? Two team options for those guys. I think there is a pretty good chance they decline Chet Holmgren's team option, probably get him back on a cheaper deal. Right now, they are somewhere between 30 and 40 million dollars over the second apron if they bring everybody back on their current salaries. They are not going to be 30-40 million over the second apron. So, what do they come up with for a deal for Hartenstein? What do they decide to do with Dort? What do they do in a Cason Wallace extension? What do they do to try to upgrade this roster to try to take on this Spurs team? Because as you know, the Spurs are young, they are only going to get better, they have a lot of assets, and this crew is all going to be here. You know what you are chasing trying to beat Victor Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Denver Nuggets face difficult roster choices regarding Peyton Watson
quotes.excerpt: Is Denver going to have to tear down their roster because they are cheap in order to keep Peyton Watson?

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
text_blocks.text: I think along those same lines, I am thinking about Denver. You have still one of the best players in the world in Nikola Jokic. You have a very good supporting cast with one of those players you were without this postseason, Peyton Watson, who looked like a future All-Star in the weeks Jokic was out. How much do you trust that? How much is a team going to try to pay him in restricted free agency? Is Denver going to have to tear down their roster because they are cheap in order to keep Peyton Watson, or are they just going to let Peyton Watson talk and say, you know what, you are overpaying him?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: Will somebody think they can overpay him and get him out of Denver since we know Denver is not going to go deep into the aprons?

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic's potential supermax extension remains a major question
quotes.excerpt: Is Nikola Jokic going to sign to supermax extension? He has not said I am signing it.
quotes.quote: Is Nikola Jokic going to sign to supermax extension? Now, he has said he wants to be in Denver forever, but a few years ago when he had the first chance to sign the extension, what did he do? He said, I am going to sign the extension, and then he signed it. He has not said, I am going to sign the extension. So, the first question for me for Denver is, is he going to sign the extension? Now, he may be over in Serbia and just sign the thing on July 1st. But that to me is one of the biggest questions of the whole summer.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Milwaukee Bucks face pivotal offseason regarding Giannis Antetokounmpo's future
quotes.excerpt: If Giannis Antetokounmpo does get traded, that is the single biggest domino short of Nikola Jokic.
quotes.quote: We will go to Milwaukee. Unfortunately, we are back in this same circular thing with Giannis Antetokounmpo. Will he get traded? Will he not get traded? Obviously, if Giannis does get traded, that is the single biggest domino short of Nikola Jokic that could really change in the league this summer. When you go back to Taylor Jenkins' introductory press conference, Jimmy Haslam, the co-owner of the Bucks, to me laid it out pretty clearly. They are either going to trade Giannis by the draft or they are going to pivot and make moves to try to keep Giannis.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Atlanta Hawks have a valuable asset with the eighth pick
quotes.excerpt: They made a huge trade getting rid of Trae Young. They are in a great spot.
quotes.quote: The team that I feel like nobody ever talks about is Atlanta. They just made the playoffs. They had a really good year. They made a huge trade getting rid of Trae Young. CJ McCollum had a great year. They had the most improved player in Jalen Johnson. They are in a great spot and they have the eighth pick this year. That is a spot in this year's draft which is pretty loaded. I think Atlanta is in a position to either let's keep building, let's not rush things, or to be in a spot where it is like, hey, we have this highly valuable asset, we have multiple picks, let's do something.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA draft value is shifting toward using picks for impact players
quotes.excerpt: If people really value the picks, let's use them to go get impact players.
quotes.quote: If people really value the picks, let's use them to go get impact players. Because an average pick now has more value than it did before because there is a higher chance of it jumping up. On the other hand, you could see teams say, well, because there is a higher chance of a jumping up, we are going to really rein it in and wait and see, especially because we do not know this is only going to be the system for a couple of years.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Detroit Pistons face critical roster decisions for Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: What are they going to do with Ausar Thompson as an extension? What are they going to do with Jalen Duren?
quotes.quote: They have a ton of big questions to answer. What are they going to do with Ausar Thompson as an extension? What are they going to do with Jalen Duren as a restricted free agent? Are they going to make a big move to try to add another perimeter creator? The team that beat them, Cleveland Cavaliers, what are they going to do? I think they are going to get a deal done with James Harden, but they have to get this Donovan Mitchell extension done. They have to decide are they going forward with this group or are they going to radically change it? There is really only one way to do that, which is trading Evan Mobley.
